parole.significato: Related to the Andaman Islands, or to their people or languages.
parole.testo: Probably from Malay Handuman, further derived from Sanskrit हनुमान् (hanumān).

parole.significato: A tree of species Pterocarpus indicus, the source of a desirable tropical hardwood, of southeast Asia.
parole.testo: From Malay angsana, from Sanskrit असन (asana).
Semantic extension from Malay jambu, which originated from Sanskrit जम्बु (jambu, “a fruit or a blood pear”).

parole.significato: A traditional scrap dealer or rag-and-bone man who visits residential zones to collect unwanted items.
parole.testo: From Malay karung guni (“gunny sack”); guni is derived from Sanskrit गोणी (goṇī). Doublet of gunny.
From Malay Keling, from Sanskrit कलिङ्ग (kaliṅga), a historical region of India.

parole.significato: A container of Asian derivation, usually handleless, used to hold liquid with a broad opening on top for inserting liqu…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Malay kendi, from Sanskrit कुण्ड (kuṇḍa) or कुण्डिक (kuṇḍika, “water pot”).

parole.significato: A constituent state of Indonesia when it was under Dutch control.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Malay negara, from Sanskrit नगर (nagara, “city”). Doublet of Angkor and Nagari.

parole.significato: To make or become like Singapore.
parole.testo: From Singapore + -ize. The former is from Malay Singapura, from Sanskrit सिंहपुर (siṃhá-pura), from सिंह (siṃha, “lion”) + पुर (pura, “city”).

parole.significato: A domestic cat of a small breed with large eyes and ears, brown ticked coat and blunt tail.
parole.testo: Derived from Malay Singapura, from Sanskrit सिंहपुर (siṃhá-pura), from सिंह (siṃha, “lion”) + पुर (pura, “city”).

parole.significato: A small mosque or other Islamic assembly building in parts of Sumatra and the Malay peninsula.
parole.testo: From Malay surau, possibly from Sanskrit सुरौकस् (suraukas, “abode of the gods”).
